comments.body: Pushed Gerrit change 1144 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1144). Implements 9305 rec #1: _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S=3600 backstop applied to the five refuse-without-proof branches in _mkdir_lock_is_stale (absent/unreadable stamp, malformed v2, foreign host, cross-namespace-without-fcntl, non-numeric pid), plus holder+age WARNING disclosure in _reclaim_mkdir_lock. Live-pid probe deliberately NOT age-overridden (never-on-a-timer-alone); macOS start-time gap left to rec #6. New test tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py (RED->GREEN + safety boundaries); existing lock suites unchanged and green; make lint/typecheck clean; lock.py 577 LOC. Local suite has one PRE-EXISTING unrelated failure in rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py (e369 area, fails on untouched base). Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

compiled_state.description:
## Why

rebar's `_store/lock.py` mkdir-lock reclamation (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale`) is deliberately
conservative: every branch that cannot POSITIVELY prove the owner is a dead same-host process
returns `False` (never reclaim) — the "refuse without proof" contract of bug yaw-gravel-linen.
304e (castoff-tigerseye-ammonite) fixed ONE instance of the resulting failure — a container
recreate making a same-host orphan look foreign — but left the CLASS open: an absent/unreadable
owner stamp, a malformed v2 stamp, a genuinely foreign-host stamp on a shared filesystem, or a
cross-namespace stamp seen without the fcntl proof all still wedge the store PERMANENTLY, exactly
as the 2026-07-31 production incident did (review-bot boot 62s vs a 30s health check).

The 9305 OSS research (rec #1, highest value, fully backed) prescribes the missing piece: a
wall-clock AGE CEILING, following git gc's gc.pid 12h precedent (builtin/gc.c) — a stamp we cannot
prove orphaned is respected UNTIL a generous ceiling, then reclaimed, so the store can never wedge
forever. rebar holds the write lock only for a single event append (seconds), so the ceiling can be
far tighter than git's 12h.

## What / Approach

Add `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` (1 hour) and reclaim a contended mkdir lock, even without proof of
death, once its lock-dir mtime (the acquisition time; the stamp is never refreshed) exceeds the
ceiling — but ONLY on the branches that today refuse for LACK of a liveness signal:
absent/unreadable stamp, malformed v2 stamp, foreign host identity, cross-namespace without the
fcntl proof, and non-numeric pid.

The ceiling must NOT override a positive `pid alive` probe. Per the research's own rule — "if you
ever break a lock, do it under a conservative fail-closed guard PLUS a wall-clock backstop, NEVER ON
A TIMER ALONE" — a branch where `os.kill(pid,0)` says the owner is alive keeps returning `False`
regardless of age. The macOS "pid alive but start-time unconfirmable" gap is a SEPARATE research
recommendation (#6, start-time fallback) and is explicitly out of scope here.

Reclaiming an unprovable-but-aged lock is noteworthy, so `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` logs the holder stamp
and the dir age at WARNING (research rec #8, "report the holder"), turning a silent 60s wedge into an
observable, attributable reclaim.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — the ceiling constant, an age helper, the age backstop on the
  refuse-without-proof branches, and holder-disclosure logging on reclaim.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py` — new.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An aged-out mkdir lock with an ABSENT/unreadable owner stamp is reclaimed (was permanent):
      `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returns True once the dir mtime exceeds the ceiling, and `acquire`
      succeeds promptly.
- [ ] An aged-out FOREIGN-host v2 stamp and an aged-out MALFORMED v2 stamp are likewise reclaimed,
      while the SAME stamps with a fresh mtime are still refused — proving only age, not identity,
      changed the decision.
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose stamped pid is a LIVE same-host, same-namespace, start-time-matching
      owner is NEVER reclaimed even when its mtime exceeds the ceiling (proof of life beats age).
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose pid probes ALIVE but whose start time is unconfirmable is NOT reclaimed
      by the ceiling (the "never on a timer alone" boundary; macOS start-time is rec #6, not here).
- [ ] `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` emits a WARNING naming the reclaimed owner stamp and the dir age.
- [ ] The existing lock suites (`test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, `test_lock_container_recreate.py`)
      still pass unchanged — fresh (non-aged) orphans keep their current behaviour.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
